translations.text: The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and his anointed one. Musical interlude.
The Lord has heard my plea; the Lord has accepted my prayer.
An assembly of peoples will surround you, and for its sake return on high.
The Lord will judge the peoples. Judge me, Lord, according to my righteousness and according to the innocence within me.
If you do not turn back, he will sharpen his sword. He has drawn his bow and made it ready.
He lies in ambush in a hidden place, like a lion in its den, to seize a poor person as he drags him away.
You see, for you pay attention to suffering and anger, so that they may be placed in your hands. The poor person will entrust himself to you; you are the one who helps the orphan.
Judge the orphan and the oppressed, so that a human being may no longer boast on the earth.
He will rain snares upon sinners. Fire, sulfur, and a stormy wind are the portion of their cup.
But I have put my hope in your mercy. My heart will rejoice in your salvation. I will sing to the Lord, who has done good to me, and I will sing praises to the name of the Lord Most High.
He has not lent his money at interest or accepted a bribe against the holy ones. Whoever does these things will never be shaken.
Measuring lines have fallen to me in excellent places; indeed, my inheritance is secure for me.
I will bless the Lord, who has instructed me. Even at night my kidneys will teach me.
I kept seeing the Lord before me at all times. Because he is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
With praise I will call upon the Lord, and I will be saved from my enemies.
Now I know that the Lord has saved his anointed one. He will hear you from his holy heaven; the salvation of your right hand is mighty.
These rely on chariots, and those on horses, but we will boast in the name of the Lord our God.
But you dwell among the holy ones, the praise of Israel.
Our ancestors trusted in you; they trusted, and you rescued them.
This person will receive a blessing from the Lord and mercy from God his Savior.
Who is this King of glory? The Lord, strong and mighty, the Lord who is powerful in battle. Musical interlude.
Examine me, Lord, and test me; refine my kidneys and my heart.
Even if an army encamps against me, my heart will not be afraid. Even if war rises against me, I will remain confident in this.
Save your people and bless your inheritance. Shepherd them and lift them up forever.
The voice of the Lord breaks the cedars; the Lord will break the cedars of Lebanon.
Lord, by your will you gave strength to my beauty. But you turned your face away, and I became troubled.
My allotted times are in your hands. Save me from the hand of my enemies and those who pursue me.
Let your face shine upon your servant. Save me by your mercy.
For the director. By David, the servant of the Lord.
He thought about lawlessness on his bed. He stood on every evil path, and he did not hate wickedness.
Your righteousness is like the mountains of God; your judgments are like the great deep. You will save people and animals, Lord.
The mouth of the righteous person will meditate on wisdom, and his tongue will speak of justice.
I saw the ungodly man exalting himself and rising up like the cedars of Lebanon.
The salvation of the righteous comes from the Lord, and he is their strength in their time of distress.
There is no healing in my flesh because of your anger; there is no peace in my bones because of my sins.
I have trusted in you. You are the one who will listen to me, Lord my God.
For I will declare my lawlessness, and I will be concerned about my sin.
I said, “I will guard my ways so that I do not sin with my tongue.” I placed a guard at my mouth while the sinner stood before me.
Now, who is my hope? Is it not the Lord? And is not my support with you?
Let those who say to me, “Well done! Well done!” be put to shame immediately.
Let everyone who seeks you rejoice and be glad in you, Lord. Let those who always love your salvation say at all times, “May the Lord be exalted!”
I will say to my God, “You are the one who receives me. Why have you forgotten me? Why have you abandoned me? And why do I walk in sorrow while my enemy oppresses me?”
Listen, my daughter, and look and incline your ear. Forget your people and your father’s house.
We were thinking of you, God, because of your mercy in the midst of your people.
Let Mount Zion be glad, and let the daughters of Judea rejoice because of your judgments, Lord.
I will incline my ear to a parable; I will explain my riddle with a harp.
He will join the generation of his ancestors, and he will never see the light.
You sat speaking against your brother, and you placed a stumbling block in the way of your mother’s son.
When Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, “David has come to the house of Ahimelech.”
I will give thanks to you forever because you have acted for me, and I will wait for your mercy, for it is good in the presence of your holy ones.
Will not all those who do evil understand—those who devour my people like a meal of bread? They have not called on God.
Save me, my God, by your name, and judge me by your power.
But you, God, will bring them down into the pit of destruction. Bloodthirsty and deceitful people will not reach half their days. But I will trust in you, Lord.
Will you save them for nothing? God, you will bring down the nations in your anger.
I will praise my God with my words. I will praise my God with my words.
He saved my soul. I lay down troubled among lion cubs. The teeth of human beings are weapons and arrows, and their tongue is a sharp sword.
The righteous person will rejoice when he sees the punishment of the ungodly. He will wash his hands in the sinner’s blood.
For the end. Do not destroy. What he wrote on the pillar, for David, when Saul sent men to watch his house to kill him.
You, Lord, will laugh at them. You will mock every nation.
For the end. For those who will change. Again, David’s inscription on a pillar, for succession.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine. Ephraim is the strength of my head. Judah is my king.
For he is God, my Savior, the one who receives me to himself. I will not be greatly shaken.
The psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Idumea.
This is how I appeared to you in the sanctuary, to see your power and your glory.
All who fear God, come and listen, and I will tell you what the Lord my God has done for my soul.
If I have seen injustice in my heart, do not let the Lord listen to me.
The rulers went ahead, close to the singers, among the young women playing tambourines.
For the end. For those who will change. The psalm of David.
For they pursued the one you struck, and they added to the pain of his flesh.
Add lawlessness to their lawlessness, and do not let them enter into your righteousness.
Let those who say to me, “Well done! Well done!” turn back immediately and be ashamed.
Let everyone who seeks you rejoice and be glad in you. Let those who love your salvation always say, “May God be exalted!”
Even in my old age and advanced years, God, do not abandon me until I proclaim your arm’s strength to the whole coming generation.
I was being whipped all day long, and my rebuke came in the morning.
For look, those who are far from you will perish. You have wiped out everyone who acts wickedly before you.
God, we will give thanks to you; we will give thanks to you and call on your name.
He inspires fear and takes away the spirit of rulers; he inspires fear in all the kings of the earth.
For the director, according to Jeduthun. A psalm of Asaph.
Your way, God, comes forth in the sanctuary. Who is a great god like our God?
He split the sea and brought them out; he made the waters stand like a wineskin.
Because he struck a rock, waters poured out and streams flowed. Can he also give us bread or prepare a table for his people?
He struck his enemies from behind; he gave them everlasting disgrace.
He chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loved.
He shepherded them with integrity of heart and guided them with skillful hands.
A psalm of Asaph. God, nations have entered your inheritance. They have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem like a watch post.
Help us, God our Savior, for the glory of your name. Lord, save us and forgive our lawless deeds for your name's sake.
Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, stir up your power and come to save us.
You brought a grapevine out of Egypt; you drove out nations and planted it.
God, Lord, who will seek you? Do not remain silent, God, and do not hold back.
Like a fire that burns a forest, and like a flame burning mountains.
For my soul is filled with troubles, and my life has drawn near to the realm of the dead.
I will punish their lawless deeds with a rod and their sins with lashes.
I have sworn once by my holiness that I will not lie to David.
You have destroyed the covenant with your servant; you have profaned his holiness down to the ground.
Do not turn a person back to humiliation. And you said, “Return, children of men.”
Let my horn be raised like that of a unicorn, and let my old age be anointed with rich oil.
For the Lord our God is upright, and there is no injustice in him.
Worship the Lord in his holy courtyard. Let the whole earth tremble before him.
I have become like a pelican in the wilderness; I have become like an owl in a house.
For the Lord will rebuild Zion and reveal his glory.
He looked upon the prayer of the humble and did not despise their plea.
The children of your servants will live on the earth, and their descendants will be established forever.
He will not stay angry to the end, nor will he be wrathful forever.
For as high as heaven is above the earth, the Lord has made his mercy strong toward those who fear him.
For he knows how we are formed. Remember, Lord, that we are dust.
This great, wide sea contains countless creatures, living things both small and large.
Take pride in his holy name. Let the hearts of those who seek the Lord rejoice.
He said, “I will give you the land of Canaan as the measured allotment of your inheritance.”
Their land brought forth frogs in the chambers of their kings.
He struck their grapevines and their fig trees.
They exchanged their glory for the image of a calf that [?] grass. They forgot God, who saves them.
To kill their descendants among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands.
They did not destroy the nations as the Lord had told them.
My Lord became angry with his people and loathed his inheritance.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercies and his wonders for humanity.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercies and his wonders for humanity.
For he shattered gates of bronze and broke bars of iron.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercies and his wonders for humanity.
They rejoiced because they had become quiet, and he guided them to the harbors they desired.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his mercies and his wonders for humanity.
He turned a desert into pools of water and a waterless land into springs of water.
He blessed them, and they multiplied greatly. He did not let their livestock decrease.
Let his days be few, and let someone else take his office of oversight.
Because he did not remember to show mercy, but pursued the needy, the poor, and the brokenhearted to put them to death.
Let it be to him like the garment he wraps around himself and like a belt he always fastens around himself.
His work is praise and splendor, and his righteousness endures forever and ever.
He caused his wonders to be remembered. The Lord is merciful and compassionate.
He gave food to those who fear him. He will remember his covenant forever.
They are firmly established forever and ever, made in truth and uprightness.
He sent redemption to his people; he ordained his covenant forever. His name is holy and awe-inspiring.
The Lord is exalted above all the nations; his glory is in the heavens.
Alleluia. The chorus. When Israel came out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of foreign speech.
I will take the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord.
The sound of rejoicing and salvation is in the dwellings of the righteous. The Lord’s right hand has been raised high.
This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous are those who enter through it.
I would not be put to shame when I looked upon your commandments.
For even rulers sat and spoke against me, but your servant was meditating on your statutes.
Confirm your word to your servant, who is coming to fear you.
6 — Waw. Give me life through your righteousness. Let your mercy come down upon me, Lord, salvation together with your word.
9 — Teth. Lord, you have shown kindness to your servant.
10 — Yod. Your hands formed me and made me. Teach me so that I may understand your commandments.
Let your mercy comfort me, according to your word to your servant.
Let my heart be pure in your statutes, so that I will not be put to shame.
He nearly wiped me off the earth, but I did not abandon your commandments.
You are my helper and the one who receives me. I have trusted in your word.
19 — Qoph. I cried out with all my heart. Hear me, Lord; I will seek your statutes.
Judge my case and redeem me. Give me life according to your word.
My lips will speak a blessing when you teach me your statutes.
Look, the one who watches over Israel will neither doze nor sleep.
The Lord will protect you from every evil; he will protect your soul.
He will protect your coming in and your going out forever and ever.
They would have swallowed us alive; the water would have drowned us.
The song of ascents. Those who trust in the Lord are like Mount Zion. The one who dwells in Jerusalem will never be shaken.
Song of ascents. When the Lord brought back his people from captivity, we became like those who had been comforted.
Those who sow in tears will reap with joy. They went along weeping, carrying their seeds.
Those passing by did not say, “The Lord’s blessing be upon you. We bless you in the name of the Lord.”
Your priests will clothe themselves in righteousness, and your holy ones will rejoice.
There I will make a horn sprout for David. I have prepared a lamp for my anointed one.
I will clothe his enemies in shame, but my holiness will blossom upon him.
They will be like the oil on Aaron’s head, running down onto his beard, running down onto the edges of his garments.
For the Lord will judge his people, and he will be comforted concerning his servants.
He [?] Israel out from her midst, for his mercy lasts forever.
Og, the king of Bashan, for his mercy lasts forever.
If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand be forgotten. May my tongue stick to the roof of my mouth.
Your friends, O God, have become very great in my eyes; their authority has become very powerful.
Lord, save me from an evil person; rescue me from a violent person.
Lord, do not hand me over, in my desire, to a sinner. They have plotted against me. Do not abandon me, lest they become proud. Pause.
I know that the Lord will uphold the cause of the poor and secure justice for the needy.
The righteous person will discipline me with mercy and rebuke me. But do not let the sinner’s oil anoint my head. Still, still, my prayer is in their desire.
I looked to my right and saw that no one knew me. I found no way to escape, and no one cares for my soul.
Pay attention to the sound of my pleading, for I have been brought very low. Rescue me from those pursuing me, for they have become stronger than I am.
You will give me life for the sake of your name, Lord. In your righteousness, you will [?] my soul out of distress.
In your mercy, you will wipe out my enemies. You will destroy everyone who afflicts my soul, for I am your servant.
Of David, against Goliath. Blessed is the Lord my God, who trains my hands for battle and my fingers for war.
They called the people who have these things blessed. Blessed are the people whose God is the Lord.
I will bless you every day, and I will bless your name forever and forevermore.
Who gives food to their livestock and to the young ravens that cry out to him.
Praise the Lord from the earth, you dragons and all the depths.
Hallelujah. Sing to the Lord a new song; sing his praise in the assembly of the holy ones.
Let them praise the name of the Lord with dancing; let them sing to him with a tambourine and a harp.
Praise him with the sound of a trumpet; praise him with a harp and a lyre.
He is the one who sent his angel, took me from my father’s sheep, and anointed me with the oil of his anointing.
